title: Last byte of SQLite nine-byte varint contributes 8 bits
summary: The first eight bytes each contribute the lower 7 bits, and the ninth byte, if present, contributes the full 8 bits.
applies: SQLite 3 master database and WAL files
detail: The previous data groups are combined in big-endian order. The highest bit of the last byte belongs to the numerical value.
boundary: Different from the common little endian LEB128; applying the latter will cause miscalculation on multi-byte lengths or rowids.
relevance: When reading the record length in the database page, reading one more or one less bit will cause the entire record to be misaligned.
